Rounded to the nearest integer, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
question.worked_solution:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $△ABD$ and $△BDC$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237869/assets/da7cc00005fbeb686443e2075009fda7c68f6d379a8ddb924a7dfe5b60e6ab16.png)

 

First we find the area for $△ABD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10\cdot 8\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{75}^{∘} \\  & =40\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{75}^{∘} \\  & ≈38.637,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Now we find the area for $△BCD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{BDC} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 12\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{67.2}^{∘} \\  & =30\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{67.2}^{∘} \\  & ≈27.656,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABD}+{A}_{BDC} \\  & =38.637+27.656 \\  & =66.293\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the nearest integer, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $66.$
